title: The place
subtitle: A river valley carved in schist

steps.title: The valley
steps.body: The Douro river runs west from Spain to Porto and the Atlantic. Its wine region, in northern Portugal, starts about 100 km inland, behind the Marão mountains, which block Atlantic rain. Vineyards line the steep valley sides and tributaries. It's divided into three sub-regions: Baixo Corgo, Cima Corgo and Douro Superior.

steps.title: Heat and drought
steps.body: The Marão creates a rain shadow, so the Douro grows hotter and drier from west to east. Baixo Corgo, in the west, gets about 900 mm of rain; the Douro Superior, near Spain, about 400 mm. Summers often reach 40 degrees. Schist soil, which splits vertically, lets roots dig deep for water.

steps.prompt: What protects the Douro from Atlantic rain?
steps.explanation: The Marão casts a rain shadow over the valley.

steps.title: The first demarcation
steps.body: In 1756, the Marquis of Pombal demarcated the Douro and created a company to control Port's quality and trade, making it one of the world's first legally defined wine regions. Stone markers, marcos, set the boundaries. In 2001, the Alto Douro Wine Region became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

steps.explanation: Yes, by the Marquis of Pombal.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Douro lies behind the Marão, in three sub-regions
It gets hotter and drier towards Spain
It was demarcated in 1756 and is a UNESCO site
